1.say: Cut one clear plug off the blue cable. Leave the other clear plug on the coiled cable. Save the cut bare end for rewiring.
placements: clear plug on one end of the blue cable → cut off and discarded, leaving a flat-cut bare jacket end opposite the remaining factory clear plug end (in the video: dark brown table with coiled blue cable on the right side)
cutting tool → closed across the blue cable just below the plug to be removed (the video does not show which cutter jaw is used; match the picture)
watch_for: If both ends still have clear plugs you removed too little and still have a straight through cable.
If the remaining blue cable is too short to use you cut off too much length with the plug.
1.check_yourself: The blue cable lies coiled with one clear plug attached and one flat-cut bare end.
1.safety: Keep fingers well clear of the cutter jaws while you cut.

2.say: Hold the blue cable steady. Strip about one inch of blue jacket off the cut end. Leave the eight colored wires exposed.
placements: blue outer jacket at the cut bare end → about one inch removed to expose eight colored inner wires (in the video: cut end held between fingers over the center of the dark brown table)
wire stripper tool with yellow handles → closed around the blue jacket about one inch from the tip then pulled off (in the video: yellow handled tool on the right side of the table)
watch_for: If copper shows on the thin wires you nicked them with the stripper and should cut back and strip again.
If much more than one inch of wires sticks out you stripped too much jacket and strain relief will be poor.
2.check_yourself: The cut end shows eight small colored wires sticking out of the blue jacket.
2.safety: Keep fingers away from the stripper blades while you strip.

3.say: Untwist all eight colored wires. Straighten each thin wire with your fingers. Fan them out from the blue jacket.
placements: four twisted pairs of colored inner wires → separated into eight single straight wires fanning out from the cut end of the blue jacket (in the video: held between fingers over the dark brown table center)
white string filler → cut off flush at the blue jacket edge and discarded (the video does not show the exact cutter position; match the picture)
watch_for: If twists remain near the blue jacket the wires will not lay flat for ordering.
If wires kink sharply when straightened you pulled too hard and may break the wire.
3.check_yourself: Eight straight inner wires fan out from the blue jacket with no twists.

4.say: Pick up the small blue boot. Slide the small blue boot onto the cut end. Push it down over the blue cable.
placements: small blue rubber boot → slid over the cut wire tips and down the blue cable to sit below the exposed wires (in the video: around the blue cable below the fingers over the dark brown table; the video does not show taper direction clearly so match the picture)
watch_for: If no boot is on the cable before the plug you cannot add it after crimping without cutting off.
If the boot slides far down the cable it will be hard to pull up later so keep it near the end.
4.check_yourself: A small blue boot sits around the blue cable below the exposed wires.

5.say: Arrange the eight thin colored wires flat in green first order. Trim the wire tips even with the cutting tool. Leave about one centimetre of flat wires for the plug.
placements: eight colored inner wires → laid flat side by side left to right in 568A order white and green then green then white and orange then blue then white and blue then orange then white and brown then brown with tips even (in the video: held flat on fingertip with green first on the left matching the on-screen 568A diagram)
cutting jaws of the yellow handled tool → closed straight across the wire tips to trim them even leaving about one centimetre of flat wires (in the video: over the dark brown table)
watch_for: If white and green is swapped with white and orange the striped wires look alike so check against the diagram.
If wire tips are uneven some wires will not reach the front of the plug and will not connect.
5.check_yourself: Eight flat parallel wires extend in green-first order ready to insert.
5.safety: Keep fingers clear of the cutter blades while you trim.

6.say: Hold the clear plug with the clip facing down. Push the eight flat colored wires into the back of the plug. Push until the wires reach the front end.
placements: clear plug → pushed over the back over the eight flat colored wires with wires fully inserted until tips are visible at the front gold end and blue jacket near the rear entry (in the video: held between fingers over the dark brown table with orange crimper behind; the video does not show clip direction clearly so match the picture)
watch_for: If the color order changes while pushing the wires twisted during insertion so pull out and reorder.
If wires are not visible at the front of the clear plug you did not push far enough.
6.check_yourself: The clear plug sits on the wire ends with colored wires visible reaching the front.

7.say: Place the clear plug into the crimping tool. Squeeze the orange handles firmly closed. Hold steady until the plug flattens onto the wires.
placements: clear plug with wires and blue jacket inside → seated fully in the front slot of the crimping tool with black body and orange handles then compressed (in the video: plug in the jaws of the tool over the dark brown table)
crimping tool with orange handles → squeezed firmly closed over the seated clear plug to drive the gold contacts into the wires (in the video: center of the dark brown table)
watch_for: If the blue jacket sits outside the plug the plug will pull off easily because strain relief missed.
If the plug pulls loose with a gentle tug the crimp was too light and needs a firm second squeeze.
7.check_yourself: The clear plug is flattened onto the wires with blue jacket tucked inside the plug.
7.safety: Keep fingers out of the crimp jaws while you squeeze.

8.say: Hold the blue cable steady. Slide the small blue boot up the cable. Cover the back of the clear plug with the boot.
placements: small blue rubber boot → slid up the blue cable and over the rear of the crimped clear plug to cover the back (in the video: boot covering the back of the plug held between fingers over the dark brown table)
watch_for: If the locking clip snaps when covering it you forced the boot too hard and the plug will not latch.
If the boot stays down the cable the back of the plug has no cover and no strain relief.
8.check_yourself: The blue boot covers the back of the clear plug on the finished crossover end.
